text:
Maya Chen: Quick thread — Q3 GPU ask. APAC (sin-1) hit 96% GPU util over last 24h, and we're burning on-demand H100 at peak. I did a first-pass cost vs throughput calc; proposing a staged commit for H100 capacity to avoid repeated burst charges and throttles.

Samir Patel: Do we need H100 only? Any perf delta vs our current A100s on the seq-LM workload? Also what's the blended price we expect from vendor?

Maya Chen: H100 shows ~2.1-2.4x throughput on our heavy seq workloads (observed in canary runs). Latency improved too. Quick summary calc:

```
Assumptions & rough numbers (internal estimate):
- Current on-demand H100 cost: ~$4.20/hr (market on-demand)
- Estimated 12mo committed price: ~$2.80/hr (approx 33% savings)
- Proposed initial commit: 60 GPUs APAC H100 + 20 GPUs USW2 H100 buffer (80 total)
- Monthly delta (on-demand -> commit) for 80 GPUs: approx $18k/month saved after commit pricing; annualized ~ $216k.
- Upside: reduced per-token cost, fewer throttles, predictable spend.
```

Olivia Ramos: Finance will need line-itemed forecast (monthly burn with and without commitment), impact to Q3 infra budget, and the PO/ledger code. Can you attach a CSV and a clean ask paragraph?

Maya Chen: Will do. Draft ask in one line: "Approve staged commit: Phase 1 (60 H100 APAC + 20 H100 USW2) 12mo term, charge to Infra-Q3 budget. Vendor offer expires in ~6 days; requesting manager approval by EOD +6 to lock price." Link to draft forecast: https://drive.internal/redwood/infra/q3-h100-forecast.csv (internal) :eyes:

Samir Patel: Regional stock note — AWS SIN has constrained H100 inventory. We may need to mix region allocations and use smart-routing to fall back to USW2 for burst. That reduces the blunt discount a bit; assume ~5% lower effective saving if we mix regions.

Chris Nguyen: On the infra side: provisioning 80 H100s requires image tweaks (CUDA/drivers), kube taints/tolerations, and a 2-day rolling node build + small canary (10 nodes). Ops impact minimal but needs a scheduled window. Ops ETA?

Maya Chen: Targeting week of June 8 for phase 1 provisioning window. Will coordinate with eng-sre to avoid rolling restarts during critical experiments.

finops-bot: New spending request detected: estimated annualized spend $345,600. Please file FIN-REQ-2026-045 at https://finance.redwood.internal/requests/FIN-REQ-2026-045 — include cost center and start/end dates.

Olivia Ramos: Also, check existing committed usage in USW2 — we have some residual committed units that might be repurposed. If we can repurpose 20 units, that lowers new commit ask and speeds approval.

Samir Patel: One more ask: run a sensitivity analysis for 3 scenarios: 100% on-demand, 70/30 commit+spot, 100% commit. Include expected savings, risk of interruption, and operational complexity.

Maya Chen: Will include that. Quick numbers in the doc now; will produce a polished 3-scenario table + CSV by EOD today. Also adding estimated cross-region egress/network mirroring cost — small but non-zero for APAC<->US replication.

Chris Nguyen: For rollback/mitigation: if H100 images fail, we can fall back to A100 node pool; I'll prepare a runbook and autoscaler policy that prefers committed nodes first.

Olivia Ramos: Finance prefers a "no-regret" minimum ask that they can approve quickly. If we can justify a conservative Phase 1 of 40-60 GPUs with an option to add later, we might get faster sign-off. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Revised ask: Stage 1 = 60 H100 APAC + 20 H100 USW2 buffer (same as draft), but will write a minimal conservative option: 40 H100 APAC commit with opt-in add-on for +20 within 90 days if utilization persists.

finops-bot: Reminder: attach cost center, billing code, and start/end dates to the FIN request. Vendor rate lock deadline: 6 days from initial request.

Chris Nguyen: Ack. I'll confirm ledger code INFRA-Q3-2026 and block the provisioning window in calendar.

Maya Chen: Thanks all — I'll upload the final CSV + 3-scenario table to the finance request and ping @Olivia and @Chris when done. If anyone wants to review the workbook before submission, DM me. Thread id: 1769998842. :)
